memory_update.text: Add MRVL as a direct AI networking and optics semiconductor candidate: optical DSPs, Ethernet switch silicon, SerDes, PHY and silicon-photonics adjacency.
Add COHR and LITE as direct photonics-capacity candidates tied to 800G/1.6T optics, lasers, InP, CPO and silicon-photonics-enabling components.
Add GLW as a second-order physical-layer infrastructure candidate due to optical fiber, cable and connectivity supply for AI data-center buildouts.
Add TSEM as a less obvious silicon-photonics foundry candidate with announced NVIDIA-related 1.6T data-center optical module exposure.

Further passes should check AAOI, Fabrinet, Ciena, Cisco, HPE/Juniper, Amphenol, TE Connectivity, Keysight, Teradyne and optical test-equipment vendors, but they were excluded here to keep this pass to five candidates.

Key falsification checks: 800G/1.6T ramps stall, hyperscalers dual-source aggressively, CPO adoption is delayed, optics pricing falls faster than volumes rise, or customer concentration creates volatile revenue rather than durable bottleneck economics.

node: AI cluster networking, Ethernet/InfiniBand, optical modules, and silicon photonics
summary: This pass expands the public-company universe around AI cluster networking and optics beyond the seed list. The strongest second-order mappings are in optical DSPs and switch silicon, photonic components and lasers, high-speed optical modules, silicon-photonics foundry capacity, and fiber/cable/connectivity. Key chokepoint variables to track are 800G-to-1.6T ramps, customer concentration with NVIDIA and hyperscalers, CPO/silicon-photonics design wins, InP and laser capacity, optical DSP attach rates, and whether demand shifts from pluggable optics toward co-packaged optics.
